Which the Department of Natural Resources considers, for the purpose of Wisconsin Administrative Code NR 154.05(5), as acceptable is 75% of the National Annient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS) for 1-hour and 8-hour averaging times or 25.3 ppm and 6.75 ppm respectively. Carbon monoxide concentration levels referred to are total receptor exposure with background concentrations included.
imilarly, significant degradation of the ambient air quality is taken as project associated carbon monoxide concentrations (without background concentrations added in) greater than 20% of the 1-hour standard or 7 ppm and 22% of the 8-hour standard or 2 ppm.
A tabular summary of the microscale air quality analysis at each of the six selected receptor sites is shown in figure 26. According to Wisconsin Administrative Code NR 154.05(5), Indirect Source Rules, dated July 1, 1975 a microscale analysis must answer two questions:
1. Is the proposed project likely to cause or aggrevate a violation of an air standard at any reasonable receptor location?
2. If no air standards are threatened does the increase in pollutant levels attributed to the project significantly degrade air quality at any of the receptor locations?
